subject: [PATCH v2 09/12] mm/collapse: open-code collapse_single_pmd() in its two callers

2026-09-10.patch_summary: This patch removes the collapse_single_pmd() function and instead open-codes its functionality in two callers, khugepaged's walk and madvise_collapse(). The changes ensure that the locking contract is maintained by scanning under the lock held by each caller and dropping it before running the collapse. This change does not introduce any functional changes but simplifies the code by removing a redundant function call.

reviews.author: Zi Yan
reviews.summary: Reviewer Yan questioned whether dropping the lock during multiple scans is necessary, suggesting an alternative approach that improves readability and inquired about potential downsides.
reviews.raw_body:
LGTM. Thanks.

Reviewed-by: Zi Yan <ziy@nvidia.com>

One question:

What prevents us from doing:
while () {
    1. mmap_lock
    2. scan_pmd
    3. mmap_unlock, bail out if needed
    4. run_pmd
}

for both cases? It improves readability. What is the downside of
dropping the lock during multiple scans?

for madvise_collapse(), I see mmap_read_lock is held when it is called,
so it can be dropped at the entry and the code makes sure it is held at
the exit.


-- 
Best Regards,
Yan, Zi

reviews.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
reviews.summary:
The author addressed a concern about performance overhead, explaining that the current patch's approach (mmap lock/unlock and VMA revalidation) would dominate the cost in scenarios where memory is mostly huge, and instead suggests maintaining the original ratio of scans to runs.

The author acknowledged that the patch will report a drop of the lock for huge pages, which is not desired, and agreed to restructure in v2.
reviews.raw_body:
The scan/run ratio.

Once memory is mostly huge nearly every scan refuses, and a refused
table is cheap: one pmd read for SCAN_PMD_MAPPED, one PTE walk under the
PTL otherwise.

In your version of the collapse loop, mmap lock/unlock plus VMA
revalidation would dominate the cost. It is not productive.

Note that scan in khugepaged is bounded by pages_to_scan so we would not
hog the lock.

---

That makes every MADV_COLLAPSE report lock_dropped, including one on a
range that is already huge, which today never lets the lock go. The same
performance consideration as above.

-- 
  Kiryl Shutsemau / Kirill A. Shutemov

reviews.author: Zi Yan
reviews.summary: Reviewer noted that khugepaged's walk carries on to the next table while the scan keeps refusing, and requested the lock be dropped before calling collapse_run_pmd()
reviews.raw_body:
Got it. Thank you for the explanation.

Best Regards,
Yan, Zi

reviews.author: Zi Yan
reviews.summary: Reviewer Zi Yan suggested keeping the collapse_single_pmd() function and making it an exported interface for the similar patterns in madvise_collapse() and collapse_scan_mm_slot(), allowing them to be internalized.
reviews.raw_body:
Sorry for walking back on this. I think collapse_single_pmd() can be
kept and still get patch 10 to 12 applied. The reason is that by looking at the
code after patch 11 is applied, the collapse_scan_pmd() +
collapse_run_pmd() patterns in madvise_collapse() and
collapse_scan_mm_slot() look very similar. And it can make
collapse_scan_pmd() and collapse_run_pmd() internal with only
collapse_single_pmd() exported.


-- 
Best Regards,
Yan, Zi

2026-09-11.patch_summary: This patch removes the collapse_single_pmd() function and instead open-codes it in its two callers, khugepaged's walk and madvise_collapse(). The function is responsible for collapsing a single PMD by scanning under the lock held by the caller and then giving up the lock before running the collapse. The patch maintains the same locking behavior as before and does not introduce any functional changes.
